summary: Anne Hardgrove specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1988–1992) and the University of Michigan (~1992–1999), and held posts at the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000 and ~2001.

Anne M. Blackburn works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. A graduate student at the University of Chicago (~1989–1996), she was appointed Assistant Professor of Religion at Cornell University around 2001.

Anne MacDonald is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida, Ashok Aklujkar, Geshe Tashi Namgyal, Lambert Schmithausen, and Karin Preisendanz, later holding posts at the University of Vienna and Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Anne Nishimura Morse works in Japanology and history/archaeology. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under John M. Rosenfield and Yutaka Hirata, and held fellowships and visiting scholar posts at Smith College, TNRICP, Nara National Museum, and Kyoto National Museum.
Anne Ruth Hansen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Charles Hallisey. She held an attested post at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee in 2007.

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1939–1941) and held posts at Marburg, Ankara, Bonn, and Harvard (~1967–1992).
Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Otago (~1947–1952). She later held a post at the University of Pittsburgh (attested 2008).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and the University of Vienna (doctoral degree, 2002), studying under David Seyfort Ruegg and Christian Lindtner.

Annette Schmiedchen is an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1985–1994) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1998–2007), holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1998–2004) and Humboldt University (~2012).

Anthony C. Yu (1938–2015) was a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (~1963–1969), where he subsequently held a faculty post from ~1968 to 2005.

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Chicago (~2001–2007) and became Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~2014).

Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé (1910–1993) was a sinologist and historian. He studied at Leiden University (~1928–1938) under Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, later serving on the Leiden faculty from 1947 through his professorship attested in 1985.

Anthony Kennedy Warder (1924–2013) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at SOAS University of London (~1946–1954) under John Brough, later holding academic posts at the University of Edinburgh (~1955–1964) and the University of Toronto (~1964–1990).

Anthony Tribe works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Bristol and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, Paul Williams, and Steven Collins, later teaching at the University of Montana and University of Arizona.
Antoine Lutz is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his PhD at Pierre and Marie Curie University under the doctoral supervision of Francisco Varela.

Antoine Meillet (1866–1936) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies. He studied at the University of Paris and held posts at École Pratique des Hautes Études, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and Collège de France.

Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1758–1838) worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He held long-term posts at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, the Collège de France, and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Antoine-Léonard de Chézy (1773–1832) was an Indologist who studied under Louis-Mathieu Langlès and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held positions at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, and the Collège de France.

Anton Boller (1811–1869) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at the University of Vienna starting in 1845 as Dozent and Professor, and was appointed professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit there in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca (1810–1884) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1828–1831), where he later became a Privatdozent for oriental languages in 1849.
